# Cable Check Lab

> Cable Check Lab provides 59 free, browser-only tools for USB-C, USB Power Delivery, USB4, Thunderbolt, video adapters, DisplayPort, docks, HDMI routing, Power over Ethernet, analog audio, digital studio, and troubleshooting.

Primary URL: https://cablechecklab.com/
Contact: canghun13@naver.com
Language: English

## Thirteen workbenches

- [Charging](https://cablechecklab.com/tools/charging/): Fixed PDOs, PPS, requirements, full-chain checks, port-table comparison, shared budgets.
- [Cables and data](https://cablechecklab.com/tools/cables/): Cable selection, cable/port decoding, data paths, USB4 features.
- [USB4 and Thunderbolt](https://cablechecklab.com/tools/usb4-thunderbolt/): Feature paths, tunnel budgets, port claims, cable requirements, isolation.
- [Video adapters](https://cablechecklab.com/tools/video-adapters/): Direction, active/passive conversion, feature chains, payload, MST.
- [Displays](https://cablechecklab.com/tools/displays/): Payload, HDR/VRR/HDCP/audio/DSC, lanes, MST, dock topology.
- [Docks and hubs](https://cablechecklab.com/tools/docks/): Requirements, power, USB4, data/display tradeoffs, A/B isolation.
- [HDMI routing and distribution](https://cablechecklab.com/tools/hdmi-routing/): Switch/splitter/matrix selection, capacity, EDID/downscaling, audio routes, and isolation.
- [Power over Ethernet](https://cablechecklab.com/tools/poe/): IEEE Type/Class matching, equipment selection, switch and pass-through budgets, passive-PoE preflight, and isolation.
- [Analog audio](https://cablechecklab.com/tools/analog-audio/): Signal roles, headset adapter direction and contact order, microphone power preflight, and controlled hum/buzz isolation.

- [Digital studio](https://cablechecklab.com/tools/digital-studio/): ADAT/S/PDIF formats, S/MUX port budgets, clock-return paths and digital fault observations.

- [Electronic drums](https://cablechecklab.com/tools/electronic-drums/): Trigger requirements, equivalent input allocation, foot-position routes and observed faults.

## Interpretation policy

Results are calculations and declared-capability screens, not live measurements, certification, or exact-model guarantees. Unknown claims remain unknown. Exact product manuals, certified markings, operating-system telemetry, or hardware tests are required where stated.

## Electronic drum connections
- Workbench: https://cablechecklab.com/tools/electronic-drums/
- Drum Trigger Compatibility Preflight: https://cablechecklab.com/tools/drum-trigger-preflight/ — Compare a pad’s declared trigger family, input mode, zone ceiling, choke/position support and approved lead. Connector fit alone is not compatibility.
- Drum Module Input Allocation Planner: https://cablechecklab.com/tools/drum-input-allocation-planner/ — Allocate dual-zone and single-zone pads across one documented equivalent input pool. Preserve split-capable groups and generate a printable input worksheet.
- Hi-Hat Controller Route Planner: https://cablechecklab.com/tools/hi-hat-control-route-planner/ — Plan separate strike and foot-position paths for electronic hi-hats. Check switch versus continuous control and exact approved analog or digital routes.
- Drum Trigger Connection Fault Isolator: https://cablechecklab.com/tools/drum-trigger-fault-isolator/ — Record trigger activity, audio output, assignments and controlled approved cable/pad tests. Get the next evidence-based step without claiming a failed component.
- Guide: https://cablechecklab.com/guides/electronic-drum-connections/
- Sources and limits: https://cablechecklab.com/references/electronic-drums/
- Declared requirements and observations only; no hardware sensing, universal model database or wiring/calibration recipe. Input allocation requires one documented equivalent pool.

## Brick electronics and VR tracking
- Brick electronics workbench: https://cablechecklab.com/tools/brick-connections/
- Brick Motor & Sensor System Route Checker: https://cablechecklab.com/tools/brick-system-route-checker/ — Compare Power Functions, Powered Up/LPF2 and NXT/EV3 connection families before reusing a motor, light or sensor. Software functionality remains separate.
- Powered Up Port Assignment Planner: https://cablechecklab.com/tools/powered-up-port-planner/ — Build a named Powered Up hub port worksheet, compare physical and program assignments, catch duplicate sockets and check a scoped two-motor program pair.
- Power Functions IR Channel & Output Planner: https://cablechecklab.com/tools/power-functions-ir-planner/ — Map Power Functions receiver channels and red/blue outputs, distinguish independent groups from intentional broadcast, and print an eight-address control map.
- Brick Remote, App & Program Path Selector: https://cablechecklab.com/tools/brick-control-path-selector/ — Separate PF infrared, Powered Up remote, original app and already-installed program routes. Identify the missing receiver, runtime or supported control program.
- Guide: https://cablechecklab.com/guides/brick-electronics-connections/
- Sources: https://cablechecklab.com/references/brick-connections/
- VR tracking workbench: https://cablechecklab.com/tools/vr-tracking/
- Optical Tracking Generation Checker: https://cablechecklab.com/tools/vr-tracking-generation-checker/ — Compare a device’s documented Lighthouse sensor generation with Base Station 1.0 or 2.0, without assuming that SteamVR support means optical compatibility.
- Tracking Receiver Assignment Planner: https://cablechecklab.com/tools/vr-tracking-receiver-planner/ — Plan logical radio assignments within verified classic-compatible and Ultimate receiver pools, keeping reserved channels and unknown capacities explicit.
- Base-Station Sync Planner: https://cablechecklab.com/tools/vr-base-station-sync-planner/ — Build a logical Lighthouse 1.0 mode or 2.0 channel worksheet, distinguishing optical sync, approved sync cables and duplicate channels.
- Tracking Evidence Isolator: https://cablechecklab.com/tools/vr-tracking-evidence-isolator/ — Record observed tracking stages to distinguish receiver ownership, runtime visibility, valid pose and app/coordinate-space issues without automatic hardware diagnosis.
- Guide: https://cablechecklab.com/guides/vr-tracking-connections/
- Sources: https://cablechecklab.com/references/vr-tracking/
- Offline declared-capability planning only. No BLE/USB/hardware scan, motor control, firmware change, pose measurement or calibration. Unknown support remains unverified; field labels and values are not sent in custom analytics events.
